project: Pennsylvania Medical Debt Case Management System (CMS)
purpose: Turnover of project state, decisions, open questions, and legal-content status to the development team.
scope_summary: A dynamic case management system for Pennsylvania residents to dispute medical debts and surprise bills. It tracks statutory deadlines, issues priority alerts, maintains evidence chain of custody, and dispatches work orders to an internal case management API.

status_overview.overall_state: Partially implemented. Architecture and priority logic validated against a 15-account test dataset. Several scripts, tests, and CI configuration require fixes before release.
status_overview.release_readiness: Not ready. Blocking items are listed under blocking_issues.
status_overview.legal_content_state: Draft only. Consumer-facing letters and toolkit require counsel review before any public use.

architecture.pattern: Transitioned from static dataset (data/debts.json) to a dynamic CMS.
architecture.event_triggers: Deadlines are driven by USPS Certified Mail delivery dates.
architecture.evidence_chain_of_custody: Records are linked to document identifiers via SHA-256 digests.

functional_requirements.statutory_timeline_verification: Python test suite (pytest) plus GitHub Actions CI.
functional_requirements.no_payment_rule: Time-barred debts must not receive payments, which could restart the limitations clock.

work_order_dispatch.idempotency: Receiver-side idempotency keys. Idempotency-key headers still need fixing.
work_order_dispatch.restriction: Dispatch allowed only on pushes to the protected default branch.

functional_requirements.redaction: Account and document identifiers must be redacted with keyed HMAC-SHA256 before dispatch to non-BAA channels.

federal: No Surprises Act (45 C.F.R. Part 149; including 149.110, 149.120, 149.420, 149.510)
IRC Section 501(r): 120-day ECA restriction and 240-day FAP application window, both measured from the first post-discharge billing statement
Fair Credit Reporting Act (dispute duties of furnishers; subsection citation to be confirmed)
FDCPA validation rule (15 U.S.C. 1692g) for third-party collectors
Regulation F time-barred debt rule (12 C.F.R. 1006.26)
pennsylvania: Fair Credit Extension Uniformity Act (73 P.S. 2270.1 et seq.); violations treated as UTPCPL violations under 73 P.S. 2270.5(a)
Contract statute of limitations, 4 years (42 Pa.C.S. 5525(a)); affirmative defense must be pleaded under Pa.R.C.P. 1030
Insurance Department external review (Act 146 of 2022; codified section to be confirmed)

blocking_issues.action: Fix returns and imports. Compute 120-day and 240-day windows from the first post-discharge billing statement date, not from default or service dates.
